title: Failure-mode: piped git push false-greens twice — hook banner is not a transfer proof; ls-remote is (Seaworthy-Pier 4a1b92)
body:
Observation: `git push -u origin <branch> 2>&1 | tail -3` reported success-looking output twice ("Pre-push checks completed!", exit 0) while the branch NEVER appeared on the remote — `gh pr create` then failed with "Head ref must be a branch" and `ls-remote` showed no ref. The same push unpiped on the third attempt transferred normally (`* [new branch]`, ref verified).

Diagnosis: two stacked defects of the known piped-exit class, plus one new vector. (1) The reported exit is the pipe tail's, not the push's. (2) The pre-push hook's output ending cleanly LOOKS like a push proof but proves only the hook ran. (3) New vector: under the pipe (and once under a background wrapper), the push process produced no transfer lines at all — the hook completed and the transfer never happened, so even reading the full captured output gave a false green unless you know the transfer lines are MISSING.

Cure: a push's success token is the `* [new branch] <ref> -> <ref>` / fast-forward line PLUS a fresh `git ls-remote origin <branch>` showing the expected SHA. The hook banner is never the proof. Run pushes unpiped with the exit code echoed, or verify ls-remote after any wrapped push. Same family as distilled "a piped command's reported exit is the pipe's" and "the proof line must prove the DESTINATION".

Pointer: branch test/lifecycle-lease-gate-helper (PR #172) push attempts ~09:27Z and ~09:36Z (no transfer) vs ~09:42Z (verified); <scratch>/push-full.log carries the successful transfer output.
